prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1283; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's agent reporting a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant, a passenger in the insured's vehicle, reports a back strain and has retained counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss. No coverage issues identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and describes the lane-change impact consistent with the account given by the insured.

Entry 4: Took recorded statements from the other driver and two independent witnesses. Each describes the sideswipe as it was reported to us, with no material differences in sequence.

Entry 5: Reviewed scene photographs and the damage estimate on both vehicles. The damage pattern lines up with the described impact along the right rear quarter panel.

Entry 6: Checked vehicle history and prior claim records. No earlier damage to this vehicle is on file, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy inception.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the initial medical records. The claimant's account of the collision matches what was given in earlier conversations with our office.

Entry 8: Medical records show a lumbar strain diagnosed at urgent care. The injury is a typical outcome for a collision of this type, and the records reference no prior treatment to the same body area.

Entry 9: Received the treatment log from the provider. Care followed a usual course of physical therapy and tapered as the claimant reported steady improvement in mobility and pain levels.

Entry 10: Requested prior medical history through counsel. No earlier injury or complaint involving the same region of the back appears in the records received to date.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file with the handling supervisor. Liability and damage appear settled, the injury is consistent with the mechanism, and the claim is moving to evaluation of the treatment course and resolution.
